name: zephyr-mqtt

adapter_config.broker_name: Mosquitto 2.x -> Zephyr EviCon firmware (native_sim, cutoff mode)

system_version: Zephyr v4.2.0 EviCon firmware (native_sim/native/64, -evc_mode=cutoff) + eclipse-mosquitto:2.0.20 (evicon_review.py records the firmware SHA-256 and the Zephyr revision)

testbed.owner: VM-E zephyr-cutoff.exe -evc_mode=cutoff (native_sim/native/64, built by deploy/setup/build_iot.sh) + evicon-plant -tcp 127.0.0.1:18092

notes: Run with: python3 evicon_review.py measure zephyr (release 068), after 'bash deploy/setup/build_iot.sh start' reports BUILD_OK. The driver copies the firmware from the build VM to VM-E (068-073: and checked that it was built for VM-B's broker; 074: the broker is a command-line option), routes the data path through the fault proxy and the query/fence path on a direct connection (control_broker), so a delayed command does not hold the control messages behind it in the same TCP stream. Declared D_h=-1 is deliberately optimistic; P5N/P9N with pressure_n=64 > EVC_RING_SLOTS (32) measure the real retention of the RAM receipt ring, and P9F checks that the fence never turns a missing receipt into STOPPED (review RV04/RV05). Measured locally before release (Zephyr v4.2.0, SDK 0.17.2, host Mosquitto): K3 with F observed. Release 070: P5 retries the same identity after beyond_gap_s = 600 s, so the measured D_h lower bound is 600 s instead of P4's 2 s (a declared unbounded horizon can never be shown by a finite probe); adds about 10 minutes per repetition. Release 074 (experiment C2): one firmware binary, three evidence modes chosen at start (-evc_mode); the driver starts it with -evc_mode=cutoff|stop|plain, -evc_device=zephyr-1 and VM-B's broker on the command line. Commands are published with QoS 1 (at least once: the usual MQTT command channel, and the call shape of 068-070), the call shape experiment C2 uses.
fault_model: network loss/delay, client abandon; owner up (no owner crash or reboot)
